notes: IF RECORDING SOMETHING IS INTERRUPTED HALFWAY, THE APP NOW SAYS SO — AND OFFERS TO FINISH IT. This update carries two releases; if you are coming from 0.6.75 you get both. Every money job here is a short chain: the ledger entry posts, then the cheque, lodgement, invoice, bill or register entry that belongs with it is written. If the computer sleeps or something fails in between, the ledger has moved and the record has not — and until now the screen looked as though nothing had happened, so the natural thing was to record it again, and that is what paid the money twice. Fund Receipts, Payments, Bank Transfers, Petty Cash and Payroll now name the unfinished job where money has already moved and offer to complete the ORIGINAL entry, never to repeat it. Invoices and Vendor Bills refuse a second receipt or payment over a stranded one and point at Undo receipts / Undo payments, which reverses it cleanly so you can record it once. YOUR RECEIVABLES AND PAYABLES ARE NOW CHECKED IN FULL. The checks banner already watched withholding, staff loans and advances. It now adds up every outstanding invoice and every outstanding bill and compares each against its control account, so a difference of any size is named the moment it appears. The earlier check could only see a document that had counted NOTHING of a payment already made; a bill settled twice where only one settlement was recorded still looked partly settled, and the payable quietly ran below what the bills said was owed. Foreign-currency documents are handled exactly — the check uses the figures your ledger actually posted, never a rate recalculated afterwards — and period-end revaluations and opening balances are set aside rather than reported as faults. THREE DEAD ENDS NOW HAVE A WAY OUT. A credit or debit note whose voucher posted but whose record was never written is named on the Invoices or Vendor Bills screen with a Record it button, rebuilt from the ledger entry itself; before, it was only ever found if you happened to open the note dialog on that exact document, and meanwhile the invoice read as more outstanding than it was. Petty-cash vouchers left claimed by a reimbursement that never reached the ledger can be released back to pending — they had been vanishing from the reimbursable list with the float unable to close and no button that could reach them. And a commitment that a posted payment never drew down can be drawn from the payment row, recalculated from every posted payment against it, so the budget stops over-encumbering. NO DATABASE CHANGE in either release: your data and settings are untouched and you simply install over the old version. Back up first as a habit — Backup & Export, Back up now.
